references.text: The regulation concerning the male goat as a sin offering for a leader who sins unintentionally illustrates the use of the male goat as a sin offering in the Levitical system.
Aaron is commanded to take a male goat as a sin offering at the consecration of the tabernacle, the same type of offering that the tribal leaders brought.
On the Day of Atonement, two male goats were to be taken as sin offerings, highlighting the male goat as the central sacrificial animal for sin.
A male goat as a sin offering is mentioned in connection with unintentional sins committed by the entire congregation.
At the New Moon festival, a male goat was to be sacrificed as a sin offering to the Lord, the same type of offering as in the consecration sacrifice.
A male goat as a sin offering for atonement is mentioned regarding the festival sacrifices, serving the same purpose as in the consecration sacrifice.

The letter to the Hebrews explains how Christ entered the holy place with his own blood, not with the blood of goats and calves, showing how Old Testament sacrifices pointed forward to Christ's perfect sacrifice.
